answer: Picture a sparrow that must climb one mountain path to the summit, carrying a stone from the river in its beak - the stone grows heavier with every season the bird has flown that same path, and no other bird can carry it. Each identity must prove a memory-hard chain of its own past seasons, one slow step at a time, impossible to split across clones. Ten masks from one purse each climb ten paths alone: a hundred steps, no shortcut. One honest sparrow climbs once and keeps the summit.
